1.country: Trial sites NR; corresponding author Switzerland (F. Hoffmann-La Roche, Basel)
1.trial_phase_design: Phase III RCT, 24 months (design details referenced to primary publications)
1.intervention_comparator: Ranibizumab 0.5 mg or 2.0 mg, monthly or PRN after 3 monthly loading doses (4 arms)
1.ai_function: Segmentation/volumetric quantification of ICF, SHRM, SRF, PED and cyst-free retinal volume (CFRV)
1.ai_tool_developer: In-house Roche model; ground truth annotations by Liverpool Ophthalmology Reading Centre
1.ai_validation: Trained on 1007 annotated B-scans from 53 HARBOR volumes; 10% stratified patient-level holdout; Dice 0.70/0.69/0.67/0.73 (ICF/SHRM/SRF/PED); no independent external validation
1.imaging_modality_device: SD-OCT, Cirrus HD-OCT (Carl Zeiss Meditec), 512x128 6x6 mm cube
1.data_timepoints: Baseline to month 24 (14,349 volume scans); key timepoints BL, M1, M3, M6, M9, M12, M24
1.analysed_sample: 1097 eyes (abstract; 1095 SD-OCT series in methods); MNV subtype analysis 781 eyes (819 gradable incl. 38 mixed excluded); MA analysis 779 eyes
1.analysed_vs_trial: ~1097 eyes analysed; denominator of trial enrolment not stated in paper
1.trial_relevant_question: Intervention effect (feature volumes by dose/regimen) + treatment response biomarker (volumes vs BCVA and macular atrophy)
1.outcome_measures: Feature volumes over time by arm/MNV type; multilinear regression of BCVA at M12/M24 per 100 nL; logistic regression ORs for MA development; Dice for segmentation
1.key_findings: Volumes fell rapidly by month 1; PRN arms had higher residual SHRM, SRF, PED than monthly at M12. Residual foveal ICF, SHRM, CFRV at M1 associated with -10.3, -7.3, -12.2 letters at M12. Baseline ICF, CFRV, PED raised MA odds (OR 1.10, 1.03, 1.04); SRF lowered (OR 0.95). MNV subtypes showed distinct trajectories.
1.industry_involvement: Yes - funded by F. Hoffmann-La Roche (HARBOR sponsor), which participated in trial design, analysis, interpretation and manuscript; six authors Roche employees (some hold Roche equity), two former employees
1.limitations_noted: Retrospective; no multiple annotations or independent validation set for model; possible OCT centration error biasing topography; small effect sizes suggest other biomarkers matter
1.notes: Funding/COI section not in extracted text. 'Modified publication 2026' note on article. HARBOR enrolment not reported in paper.
1.ai_performance_metrics: Dice = 0.70 (ICF), 0.69 (SHRM), 0.67 (SRF), 0.73 (PED) vs human reading-centre annotation [10% patient-level holdout set of 1007 annotated B-scans from 53 volumes]; PPV, sensitivity, specificity on holdout reported only in Supplementary Fig. 2 (values NR in main text)
1.validation_approach: Internal held-out test set - U-Net trained on HARBOR-derived annotations; ~10% of annotated B-scans held out (stratified, patient-level split); authors note absence of independent validation set and multiple annotations
1.trial_outcomes_reported: BCVA at month 12 and 24; macular atrophy development at month 12 and 24 (CAM criteria); feature volumes (ICF, SHRM, SRF, PED, CFRV) over 24 mo by regimen, MNV subtype and ETDRS location; within-patient volume fluctuation
1.main_quantitative_result: Each additional 100 nL of foveal residual ICF, SHRM and CFRV at month 1 associated with -10.3, -7.3 and -12.2 letters at month 12; baseline ICF OR 1.10 (1.01-1.20), PED OR 1.04 (1.01-1.08), CFRV OR 1.03 (1.00-1.06), SRF OR 0.95 (0.92-0.98) for MA by month 12.
1.treatment_effect_by_arm: Yes - residual volumes higher in PRN vs monthly ranibizumab arms; significant at month 12 for SHRM, SRF and PED

2.country: USA (Johns Hopkins Pediatric Diabetes Center, Baltimore, Maryland; 2 sites)
2.parent_trial: ACCESS (AI for Children's diabetiC Eye ExamS)
2.trial_phase_design: Prospective, pre-registered, parallel-group RCT, 1:1, stratified by site, 2 sites, single centre network; unmasked after randomization
2.retinal_condition: Diabetic eye disease/diabetic retinopathy screening in youth (8-21 y) with type 1 or type 2 diabetes
2.intervention_comparator: Point-of-care autonomous AI diabetic eye exam (non-mydriatic) vs control: scripted eye care provider referral plus education (standard of care)
2.ai_function: Autonomous DR/DME diagnosis at point of care (randomized intervention); referable DED detection + image quality guidance
2.ai_method: Locked deterministic autonomous AI system (algorithm details in prior publications)
2.ai_validation: FDA De Novo authorized 2018 (adults); prior pivotal trial and youth validation; in this trial retina specialist overread gave estimated sensitivity 100%, specificity 78.9%
2.imaging_modality_device: Two colour fundus photographs per eye (fovea- and disc-centred), non-mydriatic; camera NR
2.data_timepoints: Enrolled Nov 2021-Jun 2022; outcomes within 6 months of randomization (follow-up to Dec 2022)
2.analysed_sample: 164 randomized (81 AI, 83 control); primary analysis 163 (1 control excluded)
2.trial_relevant_question: Intervention effect (AI as randomized intervention) - trial conduct/care pathway: screening completion and follow-through
2.outcome_measures: Primary: diabetic eye exam completion within 6 months; secondary: follow-through with eye care provider after abnormal result; satisfaction survey; AI accuracy vs retina specialist
2.key_findings: Exam completion 100% (81/81) with AI vs 22% (18/82) control (difference 78%, p<0.001). Of 25 AI 'DED present', 64% completed ECP follow-through vs 22% control (p<0.001). No disparities by race/ethnicity/SES; high satisfaction; no adverse events.
2.industry_involvement: Yes - Digital Diagnostics (AI manufacturer) provided autonomous AI interpretations in-kind; senior author investor/director/consultant of Digital Diagnostics with relevant patents; trial funded by NEI/NIH and Diabetes Research Connection
2.limitations_noted: AI not FDA-cleared for <=21 years; some participants familiar with AI from prior study; non-dilated imaging may not generalize to adults; single academic centre
2.notes: Funding/competing interests not in extracted text. All AI images overread by retina specialist for safety. Camera model NR in extracted text.
2.ai_performance_metrics: Diagnosability = 100% (81/81 diagnostic output) [intervention arm]; sensitivity = 100%, specificity = 78.9% vs board-certified retina specialist overread of AI images (level 4 reference standard) [intervention arm, n=81]; prior youth study cited: sens 85.7%, spec 79.3%, diagnosability 97.5%
2.validation_approach: Not applicable (AI is intervention; accuracy vs reference reported) - FDA De Novo-authorised IDx-DR (adult pivotal trial cited); in-trial accuracy vs retina specialist overread
2.trial_outcomes_reported: Diabetic eye exam completion (care-gap closure) within 6 months (primary); follow-through with eye care provider after abnormal result (secondary); patient satisfaction survey; adverse events
2.main_quantitative_result: Exam completion 100% (95% CI 95.5-100) AI vs 22% (14.2-32.4) control; difference 78% (69-87), p<0.001. Follow-through after abnormal result 64% (43-81) vs 22% (14-32); difference 42% (21-63), p<0.001.

3.country: United Kingdom (26 community optometry practices; 4 HES sites: Moorfields, Birmingham, Central Middlesex, North West Anglia)
3.trial_phase_design: Multicentre superiority cluster RCT (practices randomised 1:1, 13 vs 13) with embedded prospective observational diagnostic accuracy study of AI, economic evaluation and HCI qualitative study
3.retinal_condition: Suspected retinal (macular) disease needing referral from community optometry, incl. nAMD/CNV, dry AMD, CSCR, macular oedema, vitreoretinal abnormalities
3.intervention_comparator: Teleophthalmology referral (remote HES expert review, decision within 48 h) vs standard optometrist referral; AI arm not randomised - Octane outputs on suitable OCT compared with human decisions and reference standards
3.ai_function: Automated OCT segmentation, retinal diagnosis (CNV, dry AMD, CSCR, MO, VRA, normal) per eye and referral recommendation (urgent/routine/none) per patient; simulated replacement of human assessors
3.ai_method: Deep learning OCT segmentation + classification model (Moorfields-Google DeepMind 'Octane'; De Fauw 2018 lineage) with hard-wired rules mapping diagnosis to referral urgency; OCT-only input
3.ai_tool_developer: Moorfields Eye Hospital - Google DeepMind (DeepMind Technologies Ltd, London)
3.ai_validation: Prospective external real-world validation vs clinical reference standard (Reading Centre senior grader + retinal specialist adjudication, full clinical data); post hoc vs OCT-only rule-based RS; Topcon-only subanalysis
3.imaging_modality_device: SD-OCT: processed scans Topcon (Maestro, 3D OCT-2000; 74.5%) and Nidek RS-330 (25.5%); Heidelberg Spectralis scans (75 pts) not processable; model trained mainly on Topcon 3D OCT plus some Spectralis
3.data_timepoints: Single baseline referral OCT per participant (recruited 5 Jul 2021-31 Mar 2023); outcomes to first HES visit/treatment
3.analysed_sample: AI study: 204 participants, 371 of 710 OCT images (52.3%), 17 practices; cRCT: 294 participants (136 control, 158 intervention)
3.trial_sample: 396 recruited overall (cRCT 304 recruited at 26 practices plus AI-only recruits)
3.analysed_vs_trial: 204/396 (51.5%); 179 excluded as OCT unsuitable for Octane (format/protocol/Heidelberg), 13 ineligible/withdrawn/incomplete
3.trial_relevant_question: Endpoint measurement/decision support: could AI replace or support human referral triage within the trial pathway (diagnostic accuracy vs reference standard)
3.outcome_measures: AI: sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV of referral decision (refer vs not; urgent vs routine) vs clinical and rule-based RS; diagnostic accuracy; wrong urgency/diagnosis if humans replaced; inference/end-to-end time. cRCT: false-positive referrals, time to consultation/treatment, cost-effectiveness
3.key_findings: Vs clinical RS Octane sensitivity 96.4% (92.4-98.7), specificity 20.0% (8.4-36.9); wrong urgency 14.8% vs 2.8% humans; similar to optometrists, worse than HES experts. Vs rule-based RS PPV 100%, NPV 69.2%; diagnosis sensitivity 68.1% (82.6% rule-based). ~40 s inference, 8 min end-to-end. Teleophthalmology cut false-positive urgent referrals 59.5%.
3.industry_involvement: Yes (partial) - AI developed with Google DeepMind; author PA Keane consultant for Google DeepMind; trial funded by NIHR HTA (NIHR127773)
3.limitations_noted: 48.5% of participants' scans unprocessable (device/format, Heidelberg conversion failure); Nidek inclusion not prespecified; AI used OCT only vs clinicians' full data; reduced precision; no clustering adjustment in AI study; no ethnicity data; infrastructure/HCI barriers
3.notes: Category B: Octane never influenced participant management; scans exported to Moorfields and processed offline on local GPUs, then compared with RS. Borderline A: AI study was prespecified and prospective on trial participants. Developer confirmed from full text.
3.ai_role_in_analysis: prediction model (AI decision support - Octane - evaluated in embedded prospective diagnostic accuracy study; randomised intervention was teleophthalmology, AI not used for patient decisions)
3.ai_performance_metrics: Referral vs no referral vs clinical RS: sens = 96.4% (92.4-98.7), spec = 20.0% (8.4-36.9), PPV = 85.3% (79.5-90.0), NPV = 53.8% (25.1-80.8), AUC = 0.58 (0.51-0.65) [n=204]; urgent vs routine/no referral vs clinical RS: sens = 74.1% (53.7-88.9), spec = 90.4% (85.1-94.3), PPV = 54.1%, NPV = 95.8%, AUC = 0.82 (0.74-0.91) [n=204]; urgency in referral-needed pts vs clinical RS: sens = 74.1%, spec = 87.5% (80.7-92.5), AUC = 0.81 (0.72-0.90) [n=163]; vs rule-based RS (post hoc): referral sens = 97.9% (94.8-99.4), spec = 100% (66.4-100), PPV = 100%, NPV = 69.2%, AUC = 0.99 (0.98-1.00); urgent sens = 87.9% (71.8-96.6), spec = 95.3% (91.0-98.0), AUC = 0.92 (0.86-0.98); diagnosis agreement sens = 68.1% (62.5-73.4), spec = 67.1% (55.4-77.5) [clinical RS] and 74.0%/82.6% [rule-based RS]; wrong referral urgency AI 14.8% (9.0-22.3) vs human assessors 2.8%; 48.5% of participants' scans could not be processed
3.validation_approach: External validation - prospective real-world observational diagnostic accuracy study in HERMES participants (204/396 processable; 17 practices) against independent clinical reference standard; model developed previously on other data (Topcon/Spectralis)
3.trial_outcomes_reported: False-positive referrals (overall and among referred; urgent) (primary); false-negative referrals; wrong diagnosis; wrong referral urgency; safe triage of rare diseases; time to consultation and treatment; cost-effectiveness/CBA; AI sens/spec (AI-study primary); implementation/HCI qualitative outcomes
3.main_quantitative_result: Teleophthalmology reduced false-positive urgent referrals among referred patients by 59.5% (41.1-77.8) vs standard care (24/38 vs 1/27; OR 42.0, 5.69-1901; p<0.001). Time to consultation 53 vs 89 days (p=0.039). Octane AI sens 96.4%, spec 20.0% vs clinical RS.

4.country: Global multicentre trial (sites NR); corresponding author USA (Cleveland Clinic, Ohio)
4.intervention_comparator: Intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg every 4 weeks (2q4) vs 2 mg every 8 weeks after 5 monthly loading doses (2q8) vs laser photocoagulation; rescue allowed from week 24
4.ai_function: Retinal layer and fluid segmentation/feature extraction: EZ integrity (EZ-RPE thickness/volume, EZ attenuation maps), IRF/SRF volumes, fluid volatility
4.ai_method: Multiple CNN models with integrated logic (ML-enabled segmentation platform)
4.ai_tool_developer: Cleveland Clinic higher-order OCT feature extraction platform (Ehlers group)
4.ai_validation: Previously validated; all automated outputs reviewed/corrected at B-scan level by certified image analysts with senior analyst QA
4.analysed_vs_trial: 443 eyes analysed; trial enrolment not stated in paper
4.trial_relevant_question: Intervention effect (aflibercept vs laser on EZ/fluid) + treatment response biomarker (EZ and fluid volatility vs BCVA)
4.outcome_measures: Change in IRF/SRF volumes, EZ-RPE thickness/volume, partial/total EZ attenuation; Pearson r EZ metrics vs BCVA; BCVA by volatility; race/ethnicity subgroups
4.key_findings: IAI reduced IRF more than laser (-0.933 vs -0.386 mm3, p<0.0001); laser worsened EZ attenuation (+125.6% total by wk24) while IAI improved it. 2q4 gave greater IRF reduction than 2q8 by wk100. IRF volatility in 2q8 linked to worse BCVA. EZ-RPE CST correlated with BCVA (r=0.61).
4.industry_involvement: Yes - work partly supported by a Regeneron grant; senior authors report research support/consultancy from Regeneron, Novartis, Roche/Genentech and others
4.limitations_noted: Post hoc, constrained by trial design; systemic confounders not accounted; unadjusted race subgroup analyses on self-reported categories; other biomarkers (DRIL, ischemia, HRF) not analysed; no multiplicity correction
4.notes: Funding/COI statement not in extracted text. Abstract IRF units given as mm2 but mm3 in results. Expands prior Cirrus-only VISTA subset analysis.
4.ai_performance_metrics: Not reported (AI used as previously validated measurement tool; all outputs underwent B-scan-level review/correction by certified analysts)
4.validation_approach: Prior validation cited only - Cleveland Clinic ML-enabled segmentation platform 'previously validated' (refs cited); no performance metrics in this paper
4.trial_outcomes_reported: IRF/SRF volumes and fluid indices; EZ integrity (EZ-RPE CST, EZ-RPE volume, partial/total EZ attenuation) to week 100; BCVA; correlation EZ metrics-BCVA; IRF volatility (2q8) vs BCVA wk52/100; outcomes by race/ethnicity
4.main_quantitative_result: Panmacular IRF change to wk24 -0.933 vs -0.386 mm3 pooled IAI vs laser (p<0.0001); total EZ attenuation -24.6% vs +125.6% (p<0.0001); EZ-RPE CST vs BCVA wk100 r=0.61 (p<0.05); IRF volatility linked to worse BCVA wk100 (68.9 vs 74.0 letters, p=0.035).
4.treatment_effect_by_arm: Yes - IRF and EZ integrity compared between pooled aflibercept (2q4, 2q8) vs laser and between 2q4 vs 2q8

5.country: Trial sites NR; analysis Austria (Medical University of Vienna)
5.trial_phase_design: Two phase III multicentre, randomized, sham-controlled trials, 24 months
5.intervention_comparator: Pegcetacoplan 15 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal monthly (PM) or every other month (PEOM) vs sham monthly/EOM (pooled), randomized 2:2:1:1
5.ai_function: Segmentation of RPE loss and EZ (photoreceptor) loss; EZ/RPE loss ratio quartiles as prognostic/predictive biomarker
5.ai_method: CNNs with enhanced U-shaped structures: 3D-to-2D CNN for RPE loss; composite CNN for EZ layer
5.ai_tool_developer: GA Monitor (RetInSight, Vienna); OPTIMA lab, Medical University of Vienna
5.ai_validation: Previously validated algorithms; no manual correction; device-specific (Spectralis only)
5.analysed_sample: 889 study eyes/patients (PM 289, PEOM 294, sham 306); 757 at M12, 737 at M24
5.analysed_vs_trial: 889 analysed; trial total not stated in paper (Spectralis subset)
5.trial_relevant_question: Treatment response biomarker + outcome/treatment-response prediction (EZ/RPE ratio change and prognostic value for progression and pegcetacoplan response)
5.outcome_measures: EZ/RPE loss ratio quartiles; RPE and EZ loss growth (MMRM, square-root transformed); GA growth on FAF; quartile shift by arm
5.key_findings: Ratio quartiles shifted downward over 24 months, more in treated eyes (quartile decrease PEOM vs sham p=0.0053; PM p=0.14). Month-12 quartiles predicted further RPE/EZ loss in sham and therapeutic response, strongest for EZ loss (up to -57.5% PM vs sham in Q4).
5.industry_involvement: Yes - university received financial support from Apellis (trial sponsor) for analysis; Apellis employees and RetInSight employees among authors
5.limitations_noted: Post hoc; selection bias (Spectralis subset only); algorithms device-specific; large lesions may exceed OCT field of view; foveal involvement graded on FAF; small subgroup numbers
5.notes: Follow-on to Schmidt-Erfurth 2025 (row 8) using same OAKS/DERBY Spectralis dataset; overlapping sample.
5.ai_performance_metrics: Not reported (AI used as previously validated measurement tool - GA Monitor RPE-loss and EZ-loss CNNs, no manual correction)
5.validation_approach: Prior validation cited only - 'previously validated' deep learning algorithms (RetInSight GA Monitor) cited
5.trial_outcomes_reported: EZ/RPE loss ratio quartiles at baseline, month 12, month 24 by arm; quartile shift; RPE loss and EZ loss growth (OCT) month 12-24; FAF GA growth; therapeutic response (sqrt-transformed) by month-12 quartile
5.main_quantitative_result: Quartile decrease baseline-M24 more likely with PEOM vs sham (p=0.0053; PM vs sham p=0.14). By month-12 Q4, EZ loss reduction vs sham at M24 -57.5% (PM) and -51.3% (PEOM), both p<0.0001; RPE loss reduction Q3 -29.5%/-29.8% (p<0.0001).
5.treatment_effect_by_arm: Yes - pegcetacoplan PM and PEOM vs pooled sham on ratio shifts and EZ/RPE loss growth within quartiles

6.country: ARIES: Europe, North America, Australia; ALTAIR: Japan
6.trial_phase_design: Randomized controlled phase 3b/4 trials of treat-and-extend regimens
6.intervention_comparator: Intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg, 3 monthly loading doses then T&E (ARIES early-start vs late-start T&E; ALTAIR T&E with 2- or 4-week adjustments)
6.ai_function: Prediction of treatment intervals and injection frequency from AI-segmented fluid (IRF/SRF) at weeks 8 and 16
6.ai_method: Deep learning model for sequential SD-OCT (transfer learning from PRN-trained model) for ARIES; logistic regression for ALTAIR; AI biomarker segmentation as input
6.ai_tool_developer: deepeye Research tool (deepeye Medical GmbH) / St Franziskus-Hospital Muenster
6.ai_validation: Transfer learning from real-world PRN-trained models; 5-fold patient-level cross-validation (5x); no external test set; IRF/SRF segmentation compared with Bern reading centre (ARIES)
6.imaging_modality_device: SD-OCT, multiple devices (Online Resource 5; details NR in main text)
6.data_timepoints: Weeks 8 and 16 as inputs; outcomes to end of year 2
6.analysed_sample: 205 ARIES + 112 ALTAIR patient datasets (2003 and 1339 scans); experiment subsets 77-221
6.trial_sample: NR randomized; 236 completed ARIES, 246 completed ALTAIR
6.trial_relevant_question: Outcome/treatment-response prediction (treatment intervals and injection need under trial T&E regimen)
6.outcome_measures: AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity (equal error rate operating point); balanced accuracy of fluid detection vs reading centre
6.key_findings: ARIES (transfer learning): AUC 0.87 for first interval at week 16, 0.84/0.79 for year 1/2 injection need, 0.74 for final interval. ALTAIR (logistic regression): 0.78, 0.79/0.78, 0.77. AI IRF detection agreed better with reading centre than sites (balanced accuracy 0.86 vs 0.75).
6.industry_involvement: Yes - funded by Bayer Vital (trial sponsor); Bayer and deepeye Medical employees co-authors; authors hold deepeye shares
6.limitations_noted: Post hoc; preselected cohort; small sample requiring cross-validation, external validation needed; ALTAIR only ~50% of data, overfitting, heterogeneous devices, no reading centre labels
6.notes: Different models used per trial (DL for ARIES, logistic regression for ALTAIR) because DL overfit ALTAIR.
6.ai_role_in_analysis: prediction model (with AI fluid segmentation as input/measurement)
6.ai_performance_metrics: ARIES (deep learning, transfer learning): 1st interval at wk16 AUC = 0.87, acc = 77%, sens = 83%, spec = 71% [5x5-fold CV, n=108]; injection need Y1 AUC = 0.84, acc = 75%, sens = 81%, spec = 70% [5-fold CV, n=108]; Y2 AUC = 0.79, acc = 73% [n=221]; last interval end Y2 AUC = 0.74, acc = 71%, sens = 80%, spec = 63% [n=221]; ALTAIR (logistic regression): 1st interval AUC = 0.78, acc = 78%, sens = 85%, spec = 71% [n=83]; Y1 AUC = 0.79, acc = 79%, sens = 79%, spec = 78% [n=89]; Y2 AUC = 0.78, acc = 78%, sens = 87%, spec = 69% [n=77]; last interval AUC = 0.77, acc = 76%, sens = 81%, spec = 71% [n=77]; IRF/SRF segmentation vs reading centre (ARIES): balanced accuracy = 0.86 IRF presence, 0.79 SRF height >=50um, 0.85 SRF presence. No CIs reported.
6.validation_approach: Internal cross-validation - 5x fivefold patient-level CV (64/16/20 train/val/test) within each trial; transfer learning from prior PRN real-world model; no external test set
6.trial_outcomes_reported: Treatment interval after loading (short <12 vs long >=12 wk); injection frequency Year 1 (>=8) and Year 2 (>=5); last intended treatment interval end of Year 2
6.main_quantitative_result: Transfer-learned model predicted first T&E interval at wk16 with AUC 0.87 (ARIES) and 0.78 (ALTAIR, logistic regression); Year-1 injection need AUC 0.84 (ARIES) and 0.79 (ALTAIR); end-Year-2 interval AUC 0.74 and 0.77.

7.country: Multinational (Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania, South America); corresponding author UK
7.trial_phase_design: Phase III, randomized, double-masked, noninferiority trials (identical), 1:1:1
7.intervention_comparator: Faricimab 6.0 mg Q8W (after 6 Q4W doses) vs faricimab 6.0 mg personalized T&E (up to Q16W) vs aflibercept 2.0 mg Q8W (after 5 Q4W doses)
7.ai_function: Hyperreflective foci (HRF) segmentation and quantification (volume, count) by retinal layer and ETDRS ring
7.ai_method: Deep learning segmentation model (architecture NR in this paper; described previously)
7.ai_validation: Trained on manually annotated B-scans from phase II BOULEVARD trial; validation set median/average Dice 71%/65%
7.imaging_modality_device: SD-OCT, Spectralis (Heidelberg), 97 B-scans; Zeiss/Topcon scans excluded
7.analysed_sample: 1545 study eyes with Spectralis scans (519/524/502); analysis set with baseline Spectralis 1527
7.analysed_vs_trial: 1527-1545 analysed; total trial enrolment not stated in paper
7.trial_relevant_question: Intervention effect (faricimab vs aflibercept on HRF) + treatment response biomarker
7.outcome_measures: Adjusted mean HRF volume and count (MMRM) in inner/outer/total retina, 1-mm and 3-mm; time to absence of HRF (Kaplan-Meier, Cox HR); HRF vs IRF change correlation
7.key_findings: At week 48 inner retina 1-mm HRF volume lower with faricimab Q8W (104.1 pL) and T&E (110.1 pL) vs aflibercept (180.3 pL), nominal p<0.001; similar in outer retina and counts from week 16. Faster HRF absence with faricimab (HR 1.48 Q8W, 1.23 T&E inner). HRF and IRF change correlated r=0.42.
7.industry_involvement: Yes - funded by F. Hoffmann-La Roche (sponsor participated in design, analysis, manuscript); multiple Roche/Genentech employee authors
7.limitations_noted: Post hoc with nominal unadjusted p values; B-scan spacing (~62 um) misses HRF; no 3D object tracking; VA gains similar between drugs so clinical relevance uncertain
7.notes: Initial inner-retina HRF increase to week 8 possibly artefact from turbid fluid. 6-mm ring excluded due to scan area variability.
7.ai_performance_metrics: Not reported in this paper; prior validation cited: Dice median 0.71 / mean 0.65 and specificity median 76% / mean 69% [validation set of prior development study, model trained on BOULEVARD annotations]
7.validation_approach: Prior validation cited only - HRF segmentation model developed/validated in earlier publication (ref 22)
7.trial_outcomes_reported: HRF volume and count (inner/outer/total retina, 1-mm and 3-mm) through week 48; time to absence of HRF at 2 consecutive visits; correlation HRF change vs IRF change
7.main_quantitative_result: Wk48 inner-retina 1-mm HRF volume 104.1 pL (faricimab Q8W) and 110.1 pL (T&E) vs 180.3 pL aflibercept (nominal p<0.001). HR for HRF absence (inner 1-mm) 1.48 (1.21-1.82) Q8W and 1.23 (1.00-1.52) T&E vs aflibercept; HRF-IRF change r=0.42.
7.treatment_effect_by_arm: Yes - faricimab Q8W and T&E vs aflibercept Q8W on HRF volume/count and time to HRF absence

8.country: Trial sites NR; analysis Austria (Medical University of Vienna)
8.trial_phase_design: Two identical phase 3, 24-month, multicentre, randomized, double-masked, sham-controlled trials
8.intervention_comparator: Pegcetacoplan 15 mg/0.1 mL monthly (PM) or every other month (PEOM) vs sham monthly/EOM (pooled), randomized 2:2:1:1
8.ai_function: Segmentation of RPE loss and EZ loss (photoreceptor degeneration); AI-derived endpoints and EZ-RPE difference as biomarker
8.ai_method: CNNs: specialized CNN for en face RPE loss (3D-to-2D); composite CNN for pixel-level EZ layer segmentation
8.ai_tool_developer: OPTIMA, Medical University of Vienna / RetInSight (co-author employees)
8.ai_validation: Previously validated incl. on phase II FILLY trial data; performance within inter-grader variability; no manual correction
8.data_timepoints: Baseline to month 24, bimonthly imaging pattern
8.trial_sample: Implied ~1210 (897 stated as 74.1% of entire trial); exact number NR
8.trial_relevant_question: Intervention effect (treatment effect on AI-measured RPE/EZ loss) + endpoint measurement + treatment response biomarker (EZ-RPE difference)
8.outcome_measures: LS mean change in RPE loss and EZ loss area (MMRM); % reduction vs sham; quartile analyses of baseline EZ-RPE difference
8.key_findings: At 24 months pegcetacoplan reduced RPE loss growth by 22%/20% (OAKS) and 27%/21% (DERBY) for PM/PEOM vs sham; EZ loss reduction larger (53%/46% OAKS; 47%/46% DERBY). Higher baseline EZ-RPE difference predicted faster progression and greater benefit (EZ loss reduction up to 77.8% in Q4).
8.industry_involvement: Yes - university received financial support from Apellis (trial sponsor) for analysis; Apellis and RetInSight employees co-authors

26.ai_performance_metrics: Scenario 1 (inferred current sensitivity, no patient data): point-wise MAE = 2.93 dB (2.40-3.46), R2 = 0.513; mean sensitivity MAE = 1.96 dB (1.40-2.53), R2 = 0.616; bias 0.1 dB (-0.73 to 0.74) [nested CV, outer patient-wise LOO, n=57]; Scenario 2 (with patient baseline data): point-wise MAE = 1.07 dB (1.06-1.08), R2 = 0.958; mean MAE = 0.44 dB (0.32-0.56), R2 = 0.972 [CV]; Scenario 3 (predict month 7-8 from baseline OCT + treatment): point-wise MAE = 3.38 dB (2.82-3.94), R2 = 0.249; mean MAE = 2.54 dB (1.93-3.16), R2 = 0.368; bias -0.13 dB (-1.03 to 0.76) [CV]. Unique DARC spots predicted new SRF with PPV 70-86%, specificity 79-90%, sensitivity 80-88%. DARC count correlated with SRF area (r 0.57-0.72). Rabbit VEGF model showed DARC detects early angiogenesis.
28.industry_involvement: Yes - Cordeiro and Maddison are inventors on DARC/algorithm patents assigned to Novai Ltd (Cordeiro director; both shareholders); Novai affiliation listed. Funding: Wellcome Trust

28.notes: Includes parallel rabbit angiogenesis study (3 rabbits). Trial imaging agent itself is the investigational product; AI applied post hoc. Ground truth for outcome is AI-derived (SRF CNN), not clinical. | Metrics note: Table 1 row order read as PPV/Specificity/Sensitivity/NPV, consistent with text for 6 mo
28.ai_role_in_analysis: measurement tool + prediction model (DARC CNN spot count used as predictive biomarker for new SRF; SRF U-Net CNN defines the outcome)
28.ai_performance_metrics: SRF U-Net: precision = 89%; recall = 72%; F1 = 0.80; AUC (PR curve) = 0.91 [RETOUCH 1/3 validation split, n=2,312 images]; kappa = 0.627 (p=0.001) vs clinical SRF diagnosis [trial eyes at baseline, n=29]. DARC CNN spot classifier (prior study, cited): accuracy = 97%; sens = 91.1%; spec = 97.1% [prior control dataset]. DARC (unique spots) predicting eyes with new SRF [trial cohort, n=29 eyes, no CIs]: 6 mo PPV 71%, spec 90%, sens 83%, NPV 95%; 12 mo PPV 70%, spec 86%, sens 88%, NPV 95%; 18 mo PPV 82%, spec 89%, sens 82%, NPV 89%; 24 mo PPV 77%, spec 82%, sens 83%, NPV 88%; 30 mo PPV 86%, spec 86%, sens 80%, NPV 80%; 36 mo PPV 80%, spec 79%, sens 80%, NPV 79%
28.validation_approach: Internal held-out test set (SRF U-Net: 2/3 train / 1/3 validation split of external RETOUCH data); DARC CNN: prior validation cited only, applied unmodified; DARC prediction accuracy evaluated in-sample on 29 trial eyes with no separate test set
28.trial_outcomes_reported: New SRF (conversion to wet AMD) at 6-monthly intervals to 36 mo (conversion rates 7.4%-33.3%); SRF-free survival by DARC count >5 vs <=5; accumulated SRF area vs DARC count; anti-VEGF injection numbers (descriptive); rabbit VEGF model DARC counts
28.main_quantitative_result: Baseline CNN DARC count >5 associated with new SRF over 36 mo (Wilcoxon p=0.0156); all 7 converting eyes had count >5. Unique DARC spots predicted new SRF with PPV 70-86%, sens 80-88%, spec 79-90%; DARC spots correlated with SRF area (Spearman r 0.57-0.72, p<=0.0012).
28.reporting_guideline_cited: None stated ('Consort' flow diagram in supplement, but CONSORT not cited as guideline)

No agent difference for SRF. Per 10-nL central IRF/SRF reduction BCVA +0.15/+0.34 letters.

31.main_quantitative_result: Difference in EZ defect area change (sham minus CNTF), fully automatic: 0.072 ± 0.035 mm2 (1-sided P=0.021) vs semiautomatic reading centre 0.065 ± 0.033 mm2 (P=0.025). Change: sham 0.161 vs CNTF 0.089 mm2 (automatic); 0.213 vs 0.148 mm2 (semiautomatic).

36.ai_method: 3D texture radiomics (962 features: Haralick, Laws, Gabor, CoLlAGe) per compartment; consensus feature selection (t-test, Wilcoxon, mRMR); LDA, QDA, RF, SVM; PCA + hierarchical/K-means clustering; ResNet-50 CNN with Grad-CAM (Keras)

36.main_quantitative_result: Combined fluid + retinal tissue radiomics with LDA: AUC 0.78 +/- 0.08, ACC 0.79 +/- 0.06, sensitivity 0.77, specificity 0.78 for rebounders vs non-rebounders; top feature Skewness-Laws S3S3L3 from IRF (p=0.0012).
